messages:
maria (Support): Heads-up — Acme said their webhook started failing with 422s after we promoted redwood/v7b-2026-03-15. They attached an example payload and say it used to be valid JSON on v6m.

acme_integration_bot: (automated) 422 webhook failures detected x34 in last 2h. stored sample: s3://redwood-esc/acme/3301234567/raw_stream.txt

maria (Support): Example they pasted (their parser rejects it):
```json
{"items":[{"id":"123", "name": "Widget"}, {"id":"124" "name":"Gadget"}], "meta":{}}
```
Customer claim: started immediately after the model tag swap at 03/15 06:00 UTC.

jonathan (Eng): Thanks. Two quick Qs: 1) were they using streaming? 2) sdk + version?

maria (Support): They use node SDK 1.4.2, streaming = true, json_mode = 'strict'. They provided the raw stream file from our S3 dump.

maria (Support): Raw stream (preserved chunk boundaries):
```
{"items":[{"id":"123","name":"Widget"},
{"id":"124"
"name":"Gadget"}],"meta":{}
```
Note the newline split between `{"id":"124"` and `"name":"Gadget"` with no comma.

lee (Runtime): Interesting — that looks like a chunk boundary split removed a comma. Could be our streaming chunker inserting a newline or model output changed tokenization so a comma moved. Priya, any infra traces from the streaming assembler?

priya (SRE): Pulling logs now. I see a higher rate of chunk reassembly retries around the cutover. Also a small bump in p99 stream latency (~150ms -> 230ms) for v7b nodes. Correlating request IDs: rq_87a2f3 (sample saved).

jonathan (Eng): Two hypotheses: (A) the model is emitting a token sequence that yields `...124" \n"name...` (no comma token), or (B) our streaming splitter is slicing between tokens and stripping punctuation when rejoining. We need the token-level output and raw bytes from the runtime.

maria (Support): Customer is blocked — their downstream parser fails and they asked for a hotfix or rollback. Can we advise a mitigation for them?

lee (Runtime): Short term: ask them to disable streaming (stream: false) or add a streaming-join shim that tolerates missing commas (ugh). I can also push a temporary routing rule to send Acme to v6m if they want immediate stability.

emily (Support): I'll offer the routing-to-v6m rollback and a one-time credit for the outage. Maria, can you confirm acceptance from Acme?

maria (Support): Yes I'll offer both: disable streaming + temporary route or pin to v6m. They prefer a server-side fix from us.

jonathan (Eng): Action items: (1) runtime: capture tokenized output + chunk offsets for rq_87a2f3 and rq_87a3b4 (lee). (2) eng: add a unit test that streams a JSON-producing prompt and verifies chunk reassembly yields valid JSON (jonathan). (3) SRE: monitor p99 streaming latency and error rate, rollback traffic if regressions persist (priya). (4) Support: offer rollback/pin option and creds credit (emily/maria).

lee (Runtime): I'll dump the token stream and raw chunk bytes to the incident bucket and share links. Early glance: token sequence includes `","name` in one trace, but in the Acme trace we see tokens split `"124"` and `"\n"` then `"name"` — the comma token seems to be absent. Attaching minimal repro curl for SRE/Eng: 
```bash
curl -sS -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_KEY" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model":"redwood/v7b-2026-03-15","json_mode":"strict","stream":true,"input":"emit items as JSON array with id,name for 2 items"}' \
  https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate --output - | tee raw_stream.txt
```
Run that from a machine in the same region to reproduce streaming boundaries more reliably.

priya (SRE): I pushed a canary rollback option to traffic router: route Acme API key to v6m for now. Will hold for 30m then reassess. Also ramped up chunk reassembly logging (debug).

jonathan (Eng): I'll add a regression test to the CI that fuzzes chunk splits across punctuation and validates reassembly always produces syntactically valid JSON for `json_mode: 'strict'`. If model tokenization is the issue we may need to normalize comma tokens in the assembler.

lee (Runtime): Quick note: this might only show up for streaming + strict json_mode + models that prefer newline after an object. The streaming assembler currently concatenates chunk strings verbatim; we could try a conservative rejoin heuristic that inserts a comma when two object members end/start without comma AND json_mode === strict. Need engineering review — could cause other subtle changes.

emily (Support): Acme accepted the v6m pin for now and appreciates the credit offer. They're asking for ETA on permanent fix.

jonathan (Eng): Tentative ETA: patch the assembler with safety rejoin heuristics + add CI tests = 3 business days (depends on QA). If token-level root cause confirmed, might need model onboarding rollback or tokenization fix which could be longer.

maria (Support): Noted. I'll update Acme and mark this P1. Thanks everyone — I'm pasting incident links and S3 paths in the thread for followups. :thumbsup:

acme_integration_bot: logs: s3://redwood-esc/acme/3301234567/raw_stream.txt, tokens: s3://redwood-esc/acme/3301234567/tokens.json

lee (Runtime): I'll post the token dump and a quick repro in the eng-runtime channel once available.

priya (SRE): Monitoring rules updated. I'll alert if webhook 422s don't drop after routing change.

jonathan (Eng): Adding this to eng backlog: RTT-3147 "streaming JSON reassembly validation". I'll link convo.

maria (Support): Closing loop with Acme: pinned to v6m, they confirm webhook green. Keeping thread open until eng verifies fix.
